items.title: Randomness in Large Language Models: What Researchers Need to Know (and Report)
items.desc: LLMs are increasingly used to generate research data through classifications, annotations, and numerical scores, but their outputs vary across repeated queries; the paper documents the sources of this randomness and sets out what economists should report so LLM-based measurement is reproducible. [arXiv econ.GN, posted 2026-07-27]

items.title: Debiased Machine Learning: Identification, Estimation, and Shape Constraints
items.desc: Develops a general framework for automatic debiased machine learning (DML), where a parameter of interest is identified by a moment condition involving a high-dimensional nuisance estimated with ML while correcting for regularization bias, and extends it to shape-constrained settings. [arXiv econ.EM, posted 2026-07-27]

items.title: Variational Quantum Conditional Boltzmann Machines for Time-Series Forecasting
items.desc: Proposes quantum machine-learning architectures (variational quantum conditional Boltzmann machines) for financial time-series forecasting, comparing architectures and a symmetric hyperparameter-evaluation scheme against a nonlinear benchmark. [arXiv q-fin.ST/cs.LG, posted 2026-07-27]

sections.name: 📦 Operations & Supply Chain (INFORMS: Management Science, M&SOM, Operations Research)

items.title: Doubly Adaptive Cascading Bandits with User Abandonment
items.desc: Studies an online-learning (reinforcement-learning) cascading-bandit model that adapts to user abandonment, developing algorithms for sequential recommendation and decision-making problems in operations. [INFORMS Operations Research, published online 2026-07-27]

items.title: AI Revenues Are Growing Fast, but Not Fast Enough
items.desc: Big Tech's spending on AI infrastructure is ballooning toward roughly $900bn this year and an estimated $1.4trn in 2027, but although AI revenues are climbing quickly they are not rising fast enough to obviously justify the outlay, sharpening questions about returns. [The Economist, 2026-07-28]

items.title: Tech Stocks Tumble on Worries About A.I. Spending and China's Chip Competition
items.desc: U.S. technology shares fell sharply as investors worried that enormous AI capital spending may not pay off and that Chinese chipmakers are closing the gap with American rivals. [The New York Times, 2026-07-28]

items.title: The Chips Rout Goes Global
items.desc: A sell-off in semiconductor stocks spread across global markets as investors reassessed the AI-driven chip boom and its lofty valuations. [The New York Times / DealBook, 2026-07-28]

items.title: Open or Shut? The A.I. Debate That's Driving a Wedge Through Big Tech
items.desc: A widening rift among major technology firms over whether AI models should be open-source or closed is reshaping industry strategy, competition, and alliances. [The New York Times / DealBook, 2026-07-27]

items.title: Why Tech Companies Are Poaching Top Economists
items.desc: AI firms such as Google are hiring away leading academic economists to study AI's economic effects, including job losses, raising concerns about whether corporate-funded research serves the public interest. [The Washington Post, 2026-07-28]
